# Psalm 90 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A-prayer of-Moses the-man-of God. O-Lord a-dwelling-place you have-been to-us in-generation and-generation.

**2** Before mountains were-born, and-you-brought-forth the-earth and-the-world, and-from-everlasting to everlasting you-are God.

**3** You-turn man to-dust, and-you-say, 'Return O-sons-of man.'

**4** For a-thousand years in-your-eyes like-day-of yesterday when it-passes, and-a-watch in-the-night.

**5** You-sweep-them-away; a-sleep they-are; in-the-morning like-grass it-sprouts.

**6** In-the-morning it-flourishes and-sprouts; by-evening it-withers and-dries-up.

**7** For we-are-consumed by-your-anger, and-by-your-wrath we-are-terrified.

**8** You-have-set our-iniquities before-you, our-secret-sins in-light-of your-face.

**9** For all our-days have-turned in-your-wrath; we-finish our-years like-a-sigh.

**10** The-days-of our-years in-them seventy years, and-if with-strength eighty years; and-their-pride toil and-trouble, for it-passes quickly and-we-fly-away.

**11** Who knows the-power-of your-anger? And-as-your-fear so your-wrath.

**12** To-number our-days so teach-us, and-we-will-gain a-heart-of wisdom.

**13** Return O-YHWH — how-long? And-relent concerning your-servants.

**14** Satisfy-us in-the-morning with-your-steadfast-love, and-we-will-sing-for-joy and-be-glad in-all our-days.

**15** Make-us-glad according-to-days you-have-afflicted-us, years we-have-seen evil.

**16** Let-be-seen to-your-servants your-work, and-your-glory upon their-children.

**17** And-let-be the-beauty-of the-Lord our-God upon-us; and-work-of our-hands establish upon-us, and-work-of our-hands establish-it.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **90:2**: 'From-everlasting to-everlasting' (me'olam ad-olam) — the most expansive statement of God's eternality in the Psalter.

- **90:4**: 'A-thousand years... like-day-of yesterday' — time as experienced by God vs. mortals; foundational text for 2 Peter 3:8.

- **90:12**: 'To-number our-days' (limnot yamenu) — the petition for wisdom that comes from mortality-awareness.

— EMET
